subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: What compatibility policy should OpenClaw use when `agents.list` is first populated without `default: true` or an explicit `main` entry?
rationale: The source reproduces the foot-gun, but the available fixes change documented routing semantics, operator warnings, or config-write behavior in different ways.

options.title: Gate new list writes on explicit default
options.body: Keep the current runtime fallback for compatibility, but make config-writing/setup/doctor paths warn or refuse first-time non-main `agents.list` writes unless `default: true` or explicit `main` is present.

options.title: Auto-preserve implicit main
options.body: When OpenClaw writes the first non-main agent entry and `main` state exists, add `main` as the explicit default to preserve existing sessions by default.

options.title: Change runtime fallback semantics
options.body: Require an explicit default for populated `agents.list` at runtime, accepting a broader compatibility break for stronger fail-closed behavior.

recommendation.title: Gate new list writes on explicit default
recommendation.body: Keep the current runtime fallback for compatibility, but make config-writing/setup/doctor paths warn or refuse first-time non-main `agents.list` writes unless `default: true` or explicit `main` is present.

likelyOwner.reason: The central behavior appears to originate in the multi-agent routing work and needs owner-level product/security judgment rather than a narrow mechanical repair.
